definition: Fabricate means to invent something and present it as real.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word fabricate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know fabricate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The salesman fabricated a waiting list, quoting names and dates to buyers who never suspected the ledger page was empty.
Misstate is the mildest rung, far below fabricate — a misstated figure gets one thing wrong, sometimes not even on purpose.
Doctor stops short of fabricate: to doctor a report is to tamper with something real, while to fabricate is to build the entire thing from nothing.

To invent is to create something new — a machine or a lie with equal ease, and the word itself passes no judgment. Fabricate narrows invention to deception: a fabricated record is built piece by piece and presented as real, and the accusation is always deliberate.

To forge is to fake a specific document or signature, producing a counterfeit passed off as genuine. Fabricate is wider — a whole alibi, career, or past can be fabricated — and it points at the deliberate construction, not the imitation of someone else's paperwork.

For sixty years the Hargrove diary anchored the museum's Civil War room, its pages quoted in textbooks and read aloud on anniversaries.
Then a graduate student noticed the paper was machine-made, a stock not milled until decades after the war.
Chemists confirmed her suspicion: the ink, the binding, even the water stains were modern.
The museum's own founder, it now appears, had fabricated the diary in 1921 — composing the entries himself, staining the pages with tea, and presenting the whole volume as a soldier's testimony.
Nothing in it records a life; every line was manufactured to be believed.
